title: Disk-authoritative ACTIVE-change reads (flip Query-first → disk-first) — Epic hardenTemporalReliability shell #6, root fix for worker-starvation under multi-session
success_hint:
ROOT CAUSE (verified): ADV reads active-change state via per-workflow Temporal Query (handle.query(changeStateQuery)). adv_change_list/show/gate_status/wip_state = 1 Visibility list + N per-workflow Queries (read-context.test.ts:399 'one visibility-list RPC plus one query per change'). Each Query is a synchronous worker round-trip needing sticky-cache or full-history REPLAY, consuming 1 of only 4 workflow-task slots (worker-tuning.ts maxConcurrentWorkflowTaskExecutions:4). N workflows x N sessions against a fixed 4-slot worker => the 8s aggregate read deadline trips (SOURCE_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) and new-workflow start (adv_change_create) can't get its first task serviced within 10s => create times out. Poisoned histories (TMPRL1100) amplify: they can't replay, so every query burns a slot + retries. This is NOT a Temporal scale limit — it's using the workflow worker as a read database. Enterprise Temporal reads from Visibility + search attributes + external projection, never N Queries.

WHY isolateAdvWorkerTaskQueues (ARCHIVED/shipped) did NOT fix it: per-session task-queue routing (advance-{P}-{sessionId} + co-poll advance-{P}) isolates SIGNAL processing between live sessions, but (a) does not change the Query-first READ model, and (b) introduced a read regression — workflows started by now-dead sessions sit on session queues no live worker polls, so queries to them fail 'no poller seen for task queue recently' (observed on addTestsTaskSignalValidation, tightenPreProposalCommands3). Also every live worker CO-POLLS the project queue advance-{P} where the poisoned/stuck workflows live, so poisoned replays burn every session worker's 4 slots.

FIX (Epic hardenTemporalReliability invariant #1 + shell #6, currently an UNPROMOTED SHELL — this is the missing durable fix): make ACTIVE-change reads disk-first. The disk projection infra already exists and is already authoritative for TERMINAL changes (index.ts:882 'change.json archived OR closed is disk-authoritative'); recovery paths already read change.json via loadChange. Extend the same precedence to ACTIVE/draft changes: read durable change.json as the primary read source for list/show/gate_status/wip_state hydration; use handle.query only as an OPTIONAL bounded accelerator or when disk is missing/staler-by-monotonic-marker (lastSignalAt/version). Result: reads become O(disk I/O), zero worker round-trips, immune to poisoned/orphaned-session-queue workflows, and unbounded in concurrent sessions (the multi-session property required). Mutations still go through Temporal signals (writes stay authoritative); only READ precedence flips.

SCOPE: plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts (getTemporalChange, listResolvedChanges hydration loop ~1103-1189), changes.ts (list/hydration paths ~651-855,1202-1612), gates.ts, tasks.ts, wisdom.ts, spec-deltas.ts read call sites (all currently getGuardedChangeHandle(...).query(changeStateQuery)). Add a disk-first read primitive + monotonic freshness reconcile (disk vs optional query). Preserve write-through so disk stays fresh on every mutation. Keep Temporal as accelerator/liveness only.

INTERACTION/VERIFY: (B) confirm the orphaned-session-queue signal path (dead-session workflows) still receives mutations after read model flips — reads won't need it but signals to migrate/complete those workflows might; align with rq-isolSessionTaskQueue02 co-poll. Do not raise the worker slot cap (fights the multi-session poller-footprint budget rq-isolSessionTaskQueue03/AC7=18 pollers) — the fix is to stop sending reads to the worker, not to make the worker survive more read load.

STAGING: This is a prong of Epic hardenTemporalReliability (promote shell entry order 6 into a change when adv_change_create is unblocked). Related: bl-z95vhQCP (surgical archive terminal cleanup, separate). Amplifier cleanup (recover 2 poisoned + 1 stuck workflow: fixHealthViewTimeouts, refineTestEvidencePolicy, addArchiveScaleRegression) is the immediate operational unblock, not part of this durable fix.</success_hint>
</invoke>

title: ADV workflow lifecycle: ephemeral execution + disk-durable record (retire-on-terminal + dormant hibernation via Signal-With-Start + Continue-As-New history bounding) — Epic hardenTemporalReliability, companion to bl-HiZJbUuy
success_hint:
ROOT ARCHITECTURE FIX (companion to bl-HiZJbUuy disk-first reads). PROBLEM: ADV keeps a live Temporal changeWorkflow running FOREVER per change, even after archive/close. Evidence: 298 workflows in the single `default` namespace across 9+ projects; archived changes (e.g. isolateAdvWorkerTaskQueues) still show ExecutionStatus=Running 22h+ after archive. Long-lived signal-driven workflows accumulate huge histories (observed addArchiveScaleRegression: HistoryLength 1155, HistorySize 1.3MB, StateTransitionCount 2824) → a big history + any worker code change = replay nondeterminism = TMPRL1100 poisoning. So never-retiring workflows CAUSE the poisoning epidemic that starves the 4-slot worker, which N+1-Query reads then trip over. Temporal workflows are DESIGNED to complete; running forever after work is done is the anti-pattern.

TARGET MODEL: Disk projection (change.json) + archive bundle = durable system of record. Temporal changeWorkflow = EPHEMERAL execution context, live only while a change is actively mutating; retired the moment it goes terminal or dormant; rehydrated on demand from disk via Signal-With-Start. Reads never touch a workflow (see bl-HiZJbUuy).

PRONGS:
(2) RETIRE-ON-TERMINAL: when a change archives or closes, the changeWorkflow COMPLETES (returns) — or is explicitly terminated after the bundle/closed-projection write — instead of running forever. Terminal reads already come from disk (index.ts:882), so a completed workflow does not break reads. Directly collapses the namespace from ~298 to ~active-count. This is what change fixShippedWorkflowTermination was reaching toward; generalize it to ALL terminal transitions (archive AND close), not just shipped-terminal termination.
(3) DORMANT HIBERNATION + SIGNAL-WITH-START REHYDRATION (recommendation (a), operator-approved): do NOT keep idle drafts running indefinitely. Let a dormant (draft, untouched N days) changeWorkflow complete; the NEXT mutation uses signalWithStart to re-hydrate the workflow from the disk projection on demand. The re-seed primitive already exists (getTemporalChange re-seeds missing workflows from disk). Requires the workflow start path to rebuild state deterministically from change.json. Result: the live plane holds ONLY actively-worked changes; dormant work costs zero live-plane footprint.
(4) CONTINUE-AS-NEW HISTORY BOUNDING: long-active change/epic workflows periodically Continue-As-New to cap history size below a threshold, so replay stays cheap and code changes cannot poison via oversized-history nondeterminism. Fixes the poisoning ROOT, not just recovery.
(4b, optional/secondary) NAMESPACE-PER-PROJECT: give each ADV project its own Temporal namespace instead of shared `default` (298 workflows across all projects today) so cross-project load cannot compound. Lower priority than 2/3/4; evaluate after retirement lands since retirement alone may make shared-namespace acceptable.

WHY THIS IS THE FIX, NOT THREE: retirement (2) collapses namespace bloat; CAN (4) kills the poisoning root; hibernation (3) bounds the live plane; and with disk-first reads (bl-HiZJbUuy) reads never pay for any of it. Together they make 'multiple concurrent sessions on one project' scale, which is the required property.

CONSTRAINTS/VERIFY: workflow-code changes must satisfy Temporal replay/versioning law (patched/versioning API) — retirement + CAN must be introduced with version gates so in-flight histories replay. Signal-With-Start rehydration must rebuild identical deterministic state from disk (contract with ChangeSchema). Preserve write-authority: mutations still go through Temporal signals; only lifecycle + read-precedence change. Do NOT lose disk state on retirement (terminate/complete AFTER durable write). Reconcile with shipped isolateAdvWorkerTaskQueues (per-session queues) — retired/dormant workflows on dead session queues must not block rehydration; rehydrate on the CURRENT session's queue. Reuse existing recovery-classification + disk-projection writers; do not add a parallel path.

STAGING: promote Epic hardenTemporalReliability shell #6 (disk-authoritative reads = bl-HiZJbUuy) into a change, and add this workflow-lifecycle work as a sibling Epic prong. Related: bl-z95vhQCP (surgical archive terminal cleanup, tactical). Operational note: adv_change_create currently returns false-negative timeouts (workflow starts, confirmation query times out) — this whole plan is what makes create reliable again.</success_hint>
</invoke>

ROOT ARCHITECTURE FIX (companion to bl-HiZJbUuy disk-first reads). PROBLEM: ADV keeps a live Temporal changeWorkflow running FOREVER per change, even after archive/close. Evidence: 298 workflows in the single `default` namespace across 9+ projects; archived changes (e.g. isolateAdvWorkerTaskQueues) still show ExecutionStatus=Running 22h+ after archive. Long-lived signal-driven workflows accumulate huge histories (observed addArchiveScaleRegression: HistoryLength 1155, HistorySize 1.3MB, StateTransitionCount 2824) → a big history + any worker code change = replay nondeterminism = TMPRL1100 poisoning. So never-retiring workflows CAUSE the poisoning epidemic that starves the 4-slot worker, which N+1-Query reads then trip over. Temporal workflows are DESIGNED to complete; running forever after work is done is the anti-pattern.

TARGET MODEL: Disk projection (change.json) + archive bundle = durable system of record. Temporal changeWorkflow = EPHEMERAL execution context, live only while a change is actively mutating; retired the moment it goes terminal or dormant; rehydrated on demand from disk via Signal-With-Start. Reads never touch a workflow (see bl-HiZJbUuy).

PRONGS:
(2) RETIRE-ON-TERMINAL: when a change archives or closes, the changeWorkflow COMPLETES (returns) — or is explicitly terminated after the bundle/closed-projection write — instead of running forever. Terminal reads already come from disk (index.ts:882), so a completed workflow does not break reads. Directly collapses the namespace from ~298 to ~active-count. This is what change fixShippedWorkflowTermination was reaching toward; generalize it to ALL terminal transitions (archive AND close), not just shipped-terminal termination.
(3) DORMANT HIBERNATION + SIGNAL-WITH-START REHYDRATION (recommendation (a), operator-approved): do NOT keep idle drafts running indefinitely. Let a dormant (draft, untouched N days) changeWorkflow complete; the NEXT mutation uses signalWithStart to re-hydrate the workflow from the disk projection on demand. The re-seed primitive already exists (getTemporalChange re-seeds missing workflows from disk). Requires the workflow start path to rebuild state deterministically from change.json. Result: the live plane holds ONLY actively-worked changes; dormant work costs zero live-plane footprint.
(4) CONTINUE-AS-NEW HISTORY BOUNDING: long-active change/epic workflows periodically Continue-As-New to cap history size below a threshold, so replay stays cheap and code changes cannot poison via oversized-history nondeterminism. Fixes the poisoning ROOT, not just recovery.

Lower priority than 2/3/4; evaluate after retirement lands since retirement alone may make shared-namespace acceptable.

title: Orphan-queue adopter is NEVER CONSTRUCTED in non-lock-owning hosts; adv_doctor reports healthy and its worker_restart cannot fix it
success_hint:
REV 3 — supersedes rev 1/rev 2. Mechanism VERIFIED against current build; earlier revisions hypothesized. Confirmed 2026-07-28 on deployed bundle b24452602d395b87 (built 14:12 from trunk c573070e, deployed==source==manifest by sha256, zero commits since, working tree clean). THIS IS LIVE BEHAVIOR ON LATEST, not stale deployment.

=== ROOT CAUSE (verified, replaces the 'stalled scan' hypothesis) ===
The orphan-queue adopter object is NEVER INSTANTIATED in most hosts.

plugin-init.ts:409-422 —
  if (worker) {
    registerInProcessTemporalWorker(worker);
    if (temporalBundle && isOrphanQueueAdoptionEnabled()) {
      activeOrphanQueueAdopter = new OrphanQueueAdopter({ client, projectId, worker });
    }
  }
plugin-init.ts:501-503 — getOrphanQueueAdoptionDiagnostics() returns activeOrphanQueueAdopter?.getDiagnostics() ?? null.

adv_doctor returned orphan_queue_adoption:{enabled:false, note:'no active adopter'} = NULL diagnostics = the object was never constructed. A stalled-but-existing adopter would have returned scanInFlight/trackedQueues instead. So #327's filed symptom (scanInFlight:true, attemptCount:0) is a DIFFERENT failure mode from what this host exhibits. Fix construction first: a non-existent adopter cannot stall.

NOT the kill-switch: ADV_ORPHAN_QUEUE_ADOPTION unset in every process; code comment says 'default ON; 0 disables — adoption is always-on in production; the flag is an emergency escape hatch only.'

WHY `worker` IS FALSY: shouldSpawnWorker = singletonPlan.shouldSpawnWorker (plugin-init.ts:273-289) from resolveWorkerSingletonPlan with worker_singleton_enforce defaulting true. ONLY THE LOCK-OWNING HOST SPAWNS A WORKER — so every non-owning host has adoption permanently off.

SECOND COUPLING: adoptNextOrphan() is driven by the worker-lock heartbeat onBeat (plugin-init.ts:299-304), which only starts when singletonPlan.lockResult?.owned. Adoption requires BOTH owning the lock AND spawning the worker in that same process.

=== THE adv_doctor TRAP (do not rely on it) ===
doctor's worker_restart restarts the worker OUTSIDE plugin-init, so activeOrphanQueueAdopter is never assigned. Two live runs:
  18:25:54Z run 1 -> finding worker_down_owned ('no suspect lock and no peer contention'); applied worker_restart; verification healthy:false, queue_serviceable:false; orphan_queue_adoption enabled:false
  18:26:08Z run 2 -> findings 'healthy: All checks passed'; healthy:true, server_alive:true, worker_alive:true, queue_serviceable:true, search_attributes_ok:true; orphan_queue_adoption STILL enabled:false
DOCTOR REPORTS FULL HEALTH WHILE ADOPTION IS DEAD, and re-running it cannot help because its repair path structurally cannot construct the adopter. Recommended fix: report healthy:false whenever orphan_queue_adoption.enabled === false, and have worker_restart construct/attach an adopter.

=== RESTART IS AN ANTI-REMEDY (critical operator guidance) ===
An OpenCode restart was performed mid-session to try to clear the blackout. Outcome:
  - ALL worker processes died and NONE respawned until adv_doctor was run manually.
  - The new worker polls 2 queues (own-session + project), down from 34.
  - FIVE changes created ~30 minutes earlier became unreachable. adv_gate_status fixStalledOrphanQueueAdoption now TIMES OUT (ToolExecutionTimeout 10s), and adv_change_update on it silently FAILED (readback proved the write never landed).
Because adoption never runs, EVERY RESTART MINTS NEW PERMANENT ORPHANS. The standard operator reflex for 'ADV is stuck' deepens the fault. Do not restart to clear a blackout.

NOTE THE IRONY, it is diagnostic: the change created to FIX orphan-queue adoption cannot have its own proposal edited, because its workflow was orphaned by the defect it documents. Its proposal is frozen at rev 3; rev 4 (this content) had to be written here instead.

=== NO DATA LOSS ===
All 10 changes still list. Every proposal reads back intact via adv_change_show include:{proposal:true, artifactOnly:true} — verified byte-for-byte on makeToolReadsWorkerFree. Disk persistence held throughout. CONTENT IS SAFE; ONLY GATES ARE UNREACHABLE. Do not attempt data recovery; attempt reachability recovery.

=== WHAT STILL FAILS AFTER doctor + restart ===
  adv_change_show fixSubagentReportRouting -> not_found
  adv_gate_status fixStalledOrphanQueueAdoption -> ToolExecutionTimeout
  adv_change_update fixStalledOrphanQueueAdoption -> timeout, write did NOT land
  adv_epic_list -> []   adv_epic_show optimizeAdvToolSurface -> EPIC_NOT_FOUND
  adv_change_list / adv_task_list / adv_backlog_* -> WORK (disk-backed)

=== OWNERSHIP SPLIT (established this session) ===
  CLI reads (bin/adv, dashboard)                  -> fixWorkerDependentResume (PRs #335, #336, merged)
  Plugin-tool reads (adv_change_show/gate_status/epic_*) -> makeToolReadsWorkerFree (new)
  Signals/mutations + describe-gated recovery prechecks  -> fixStalledOrphanQueueAdoption (#327)
Reads can avoid a worker; SIGNALS CANNOT. Adoption is the half the worker-free read migration structurally cannot cover.

=== DONE WHEN ===
(a) adopter construction is decoupled from same-process worker spawning, so a non-lock-owning host can still drive adoption; (b) the adoption tick is decoupled from the worker-lock heartbeat or has an equivalent driver; (c) adv_doctor either constructs an adopter on worker_restart or reports unhealthy while adoption is absent; (d) degraded reads surface a typed UNREACHABLE marker distinct from not_found; (e) a reclaim path exists for queues already orphaned by prior restarts; (f) fixSubagentReportRouting reaches a true terminal archived state.

title: Fix sub-agent packet anchor contract mismatch (adv-verifier SCOPE KEY / PHASE)
success_hint: A spawn that satisfies the documented anchor contract never hard-refuses. Either adv-verifier accepts the documented set (defaulting PHASE to local_verify), or the orchestrator template lists SCOPE KEY + PHASE as required for the verifier lane. Regression test spawns using only documented anchors and asserts work is performed.

context_packet.background:
adv-verifier hard-refuses a spawn when the packet omits SCOPE KEY and PHASE: it returns status=inconclusive, error_class=UNKNOWN, recommended_next_action=ask_user, and runs ZERO commands.

Observed 2026-07-29 while delegating a trunk-baseline regression comparison. Packet supplied WORKING DIRECTORY, CHANGE, TASK and ATTEMPT. Refusal evidence_basis: 'Required packet identity anchors missing: SCOPE KEY and PHASE. No commands run.' required_main_agent_actions: ['Provide SCOPE KEY and PHASE (local_verify or ci_check).' ] Resuming the same session with the two anchors added succeeded (two full suite runs, 707s + 783s, verdict NO_REGRESSION).

This is a contract bug, not user error. The orchestrator packet contract documents required anchors as WORKING DIRECTORY, CHANGE, TASK or SCOPE KEY, ATTEMPT - with PHASE called out only for adv-reviewer. adv-verifier enforces SCOPE KEY and PHASE as both-required, so a packet satisfying the documented contract still hard-refuses. These are orchestrator-owned identity fields and cannot be surfaced to the user, so the cost is a wasted spawn plus a retry cycle every time.

Inconsistency with its own lane class: read-only lanes (adv-researcher, adv-tron, adv-visual-review) are required to COMPLETE the work and prepend a PACKET DEFECT section when anchors are missing. adv-verifier is also read-only (edit: deny) but refuses instead.

references.label: Read-only lane packet rule (complete work, prepend PACKET DEFECT)

constraints: Fail-soft is the correct direction for a read-only lane: do the work, report the packet defect.
Anchors are orchestrator-owned; never escalate a missing anchor to the end user.
Any relaxation must still record that the packet was malformed, so drift stays visible.
avoidances: Do not silently accept malformed packets with no defect signal - that hides the drift instead of fixing it.
Do not fix only adv-verifier; the same documented-vs-enforced drift may exist in other typed lanes.
context_packet.design_seed:
Preferred fix: relax adv-verifier to accept the documented anchor set, defaulting PHASE to local_verify when absent, and emit a PACKET DEFECT section rather than refusing - matching the existing read-only-lane rule.

Alternative: update delegation-defaults/spec.json and the orchestrator packet template so SCOPE KEY and PHASE are listed as required for the verifier lane.

Audit scope: check EVERY typed worker lane for drift between documented anchors and enforced anchors, and add a test that asserts the documented template is sufficient for each lane.

title: Trunk write firewall resolves relative paths against trunk, not shell cwd
success_hint: A relative-path write issued from a nested worktree subdirectory resolves against the writing process cwd and is allowed, while genuine trunk writes stay blocked. Regression matrix covers {trunk root, trunk subdir, worktree root, worktree subdir} x {absolute, relative}.

context_packet.background:
The ADV trunk-write firewall blocked a legitimate write inside an ad-hoc worktree because it resolved a relative path against the trunk checkout root instead of the writing process cwd.

Observed 2026-07-29. Shell cwd was /home/jon/.local/share/opencode/worktree-adhoc/advance/fix-adoption-observability/plugin and the write target was the relative path src/temporal/orphan-queue-adopter.scan-resilience.test.ts

The refusal named /home/jon/dev/advance/src/temporal/orphan-queue-adopter.scan-resilience.test.ts and told the operator to create or use an ADV worktree.

Two tells prove misresolution rather than a correct block. First, the reported path is under the trunk checkout although cwd was inside the worktree. Second, the reported path is missing the plugin/ segment entirely; correct resolution against cwd would end in plugin/src/temporal/... The firewall appears to join the relative path onto the ADV project root rather than the cwd.

Impact: false positives block correct worktree work whenever a write uses a relative path from a nested subdirectory, and the guidance is actively misleading because it tells the operator to use a worktree while they are already in one. Trunk-worktree isolation is a core invariant, so a guard that misfires erodes trust in it.

The blocked call was a shell heredoc append, which is itself discouraged, but the path resolution is wrong independent of which tool triggers it.
constraints: Genuine writes to a trunk checkout on the default branch must stay blocked.
Resolution must be relative to the writing process cwd, not the ADV project root.
Preserve target-relative behaviour so a foreign repo trunk stays protected.
avoidances: Do not special-case the worktree-adhoc path prefix; fix the resolution rule itself.
Do not silently allow ambiguous paths. If cwd cannot be determined, refuse and explain why.
context_packet.design_seed: Resolve the target with path.resolve(processCwd, target) before classifying, then compute git root and branch topology from the resolved path. Today the relative path is joined onto the project root, which is only correct when cwd equals that root. Add the four-by-two regression matrix; the worktree-subdir plus relative cell is the failing one.

title: RESOLVED (PR #344): adv-verifier refused a defective packet instead of failing soft
success_hint: Done. adv-verifier now completes verification on a defective packet and reports a ## PACKET DEFECT section, with WORKING DIRECTORY as the only hard block and PHASE defaulting to local_verify. Pinned by a test in adv-verifier-assets.test.ts.

context_packet.background:
RESOLVED by PR #344 (merged 1e8ef678, deployed).

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL REPORT. This item was first filed as a documented-vs-enforced anchor contract mismatch, claiming adv-verifier wrongly required SCOPE KEY and PHASE. That framing was WRONG. Those anchors are legitimately required and are pinned as body anchors by plugin/src/adv-verifier-assets.test.ts. Requiring them was never the defect.

The actual defect was narrower: adv-verifier REFUSED rather than REPORTED. title: ADV routes mid-lifecycle findings to change-creation instead of the backlog
success_hint: An agent that surfaces an out-of-scope finding during design, prep, apply, review or harden has a durable low-commitment sink it is actually told about; and DONT/OOS contract items are evaluated rather than merely declared.

context_packet.background:
ADV already has the correct two-tier structure: adv_backlog_add (candidate) vs adv_change_create (commitment), bridged by the deliberate adv_backlog_promote. But the workflow only routes findings to the candidate tier during proposal and discovery. From design onward the only durable sink an agent is told about is change-creation, so ADV generates the change accumulation it then cannot clear.

Observed live in decideWorkflowHibernation: it measured 10.71 new changes/day x 38 percent never-terminal = 4.07 permanently-running entities/day, concluded the root cause was that entities never reach terminal state, then in its own prep phase reflexively created 3 new changes. Precision (P38): that lifecycle field is descriptive metadata, NOT enforcement. The catalog states restriction labels do not grant or deny access. title: Unregistered-signal loss is structurally invisible (rq-hib04, orphaned by supersession)
success_hint: A signal delivered for a name the running worker build does not register is observable rather than silently dropped, so the failure class can be alerted on, counted, and debugged.

context_packet.background:
A signal sent for a name the running worker build does not register is buffered in SDK memory and never delivered if the workflow completes first. Nothing logs it.

Proven from SDK source, not prose. sdk-typescript/packages/workflow/src/internals.ts:
  :194-197  readonly bufferedSignals = Array<...>  // 'Holds buffered signal calls until a handler is registered'
  :1114-1116  if (!this.signalHandlers.has(signalName) && !this.defaultSignalHandler) { this.bufferedSignals.push(activation); return; }
  :1138-1146  dispatchBufferedSignals() drains the buffer; when a default handler is present EVERY buffered signal becomes dispatchable, otherwise only signals whose specific name has since been registered.

Installing setDefaultSignalHandler is what converts an invisible buffer into something the codebase can observe.

WHY THIS IS A BACKLOG ITEM AND NOT A CHANGE
It previously WAS a change, addSignalLossObservability, created 2026-08-05T00:24:10Z. Four minutes later a concurrent agent absorbed three overlapping fast-follows into fixAdvStateAuthority and closed them as superseded with user approval. That consolidation was correct for the other two. For this one the stated rationale was that signal-loss is 'covered by fixAdvStateAuthority item 3 (cross-surface conformance invariant failing the build when any two read surfaces disagree while both answer) and item 4 (binding provenance envelope)'.

That rationale does not hold. fixAdvStateAuthority's approved contract has 15 acceptance criteria covering enumeration terminal-dominance, project-identity minting, store consolidation, abandoned-workflow ending, Epic listing, and bundle-generation recovery hints. NONE installs a default signal handler or addresses SDK-level signal buffering. The finding was absorbed administratively but not substantively, so it is recorded here rather than left to disappear.

RELATIONSHIP TO ADR-002
decideWorkflowHibernation (archived) decided AFFIRMATIVE on adopting a hibernation lifecycle state. Its DEC-5 promoted this work from standalone hardening to a BLOCKING PREREQUISITE, because hibernation deliberately increases workflow completion events and completion is exactly when buffered signals are lost. Shipping hibernation without this would make a currently-invisible failure both more frequent and still invisible.

Note fixAdvStateAuthority separately records 'Dependency direction inverted: decideWorkflowHibernation is a compensating mechanism over the primary mechanism this change repairs.' That is a claim about hibernation-vs-state-authority ordering. It does not bear on signal-loss observability, which is independent of both.

references.label: Superseding change whose contract does NOT cover this
Dependent build that named this a prerequisite

constraints: Observability only. Must not alter dispatch of registered signals, consume them, or add a failure path to the handler chain (ADR-002 DDC3).
Must preserve the signal/query-only workflow surface; no defineUpdate in workflow-reachable code.
Signal handlers must not throw (docs/adr/0003-signal-handlers-must-not-throw.md).
avoidances: Do not assume fixAdvStateAuthority covers this. Its 15 approved acceptance criteria were checked individually and none addresses signal buffering; the original supersession rationale was mistaken.
Do not fail loudly on unregistered signals instead of logging. ADR-002 rejected that explicitly because it changes dispatch behavior.
Do not treat this as blocked on the hibernation decision. The hazard exists today on paths ADV already runs; hibernation only widens the window.

Install setDefaultSignalHandler on the change workflow (and the epic workflow) so an unregistered signal name is recorded with the signal name and change id.

- must not alter dispatch of registered signals
- must not consume signals
- must not introduce a new failure path in the handler chain

So adding a default handler is not warning-free; evaluate the noise cost before shipping.

Sizing: small and additive. The mechanism is a single SDK call plus a log/metric sink.

success_hint: OpenCode natively supports per-agent instruction scoping (agent.<name>.instructions or equivalent), removing the structural need to load the full instruction floor into every spawned sub-agent.
